\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رخصة} (rukhṣa)}{رخصة (rukhṣa)}]{\ar{رخصة} (rukhṣa) — a licence; a permit}

\label{lesson:AR-C434-rukhsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a pump, then the Arabic for to tow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رخصة}}
\textbf{\ar{رخصة}} — \emph{rukhṣa} — \textquotedblleft{}a licence; a permit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عند} \ar{أختي} \ar{رخصة} \ar{قيادة} \ar{جديدة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿinda ukhtī rukhṣat qiyāda jadīda.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister has a new driving licence.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رخصة}} (\emph{rukhṣa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-kh-ṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be soft, easy, cheap\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{rukhṣa} is an easing: a permission. It shares its root with \emph{rakhīṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}cheap\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukhṣa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukhṣa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿinda ukhtī rukhṣat qiyāda jadīda.} — My sister has a new driving licence.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a pump, then the Arabic for to tow, then say \emph{rukhṣa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رخصة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A licence; a permit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منعطف} (munʿaṭaf)}{منعطف (munʿaṭaf)}]{\ar{منعطف} (munʿaṭaf) — a bend; a turning}

\label{lesson:AR-C434-munataf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to tow, then the Arabic for a licence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{منعطف}}
\textbf{\ar{منعطف}} — \emph{munʿaṭaf} — \textquotedblleft{}a bend; a turning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{المنعطف} \ar{على} \ar{طريق} \ar{الجبل} \ar{خطيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-munʿaṭaf ʿalā ṭarīq al-jabal khaṭīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bend on the mountain road was dangerous.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{منعطف}} (\emph{munʿaṭaf}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ṭ-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to bend, to turn\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the place-noun of \emph{inʿaṭafa}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munʿaṭaf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munʿaṭaf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-munʿaṭaf ʿalā ṭarīq al-jabal khaṭīran.} — The bend on the mountain road was dangerous.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to tow, then the Arabic for a licence, then say \emph{munʿaṭaf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{منعطف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bend; a turning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جدد} (jaddada)}{جدد (jaddada)}]{\ar{جدد} (jaddada) — to renew}

\label{lesson:AR-C434-jaddada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a licence, then the Arabic for a bend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جدد}}
\textbf{\ar{جدد}} — \emph{jaddada} — \textquotedblleft{}to renew\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{جدد} \ar{أبي} \ar{رخصته} \ar{هذا} \ar{الشهر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jaddada abī rukhṣatahu hādhā ash-shahr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father renewed his licence this month.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يجدد}, \emph{yujaddid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جدد}} (\emph{jaddada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to be new\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to make new\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{jadīd}, \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jaddada}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a licence, then the Arabic for a bend, then say \emph{jaddada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أصدر} (aṣdara)}{أصدر (aṣdara)}]{\ar{أصدر} (aṣdara) — to issue}

\label{lesson:AR-C434-asdara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bend, then the Arabic for to renew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أصدر}}
\textbf{\ar{أصدر}} — \emph{aṣdara} — \textquotedblleft{}to issue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أصدرت} \ar{السفارة} \ar{التأشيرة} \ar{بعد} \ar{أسبوع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṣdarat as-sifāra at-taʾshīra baʿda usbūʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The embassy issued the visa after a week.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصدر}, \emph{yuṣdir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أصدر}} (\emph{aṣdara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-d-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to come forth\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to send forth\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تجاوز} (tajāwaza)}{تجاوز (tajāwaza)}]{\ar{تجاوز} (tajāwaza) — to overtake; to exceed}

\label{lesson:AR-C434-tajawaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to renew, then the Arabic for to issue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تجاوز}}
\textbf{\ar{تجاوز}} — \emph{tajāwaza} — \textquotedblleft{}to overtake; to exceed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تجاوزت} \ar{سيارة} \ar{الحافلة} \ar{على} \ar{الجسر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tajāwazat sayyāra al-ḥāfila ʿalā al-jisr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A car overtook the bus on the bridge.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتجاوز}, \emph{yatajāwaz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تجاوز}} (\emph{tajāwaza}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-w-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass beyond\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI; \emph{jawāz}, \textquotedblleft{}a passport\textquotedblright{}, is a permit to pass.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to renew, then the Arabic for to issue, then say \emph{tajāwaza} again
\end{itemize}
